journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

guards.title: Clicking the date field still shows the calendar
guards.goal: A pointer user who clicks the departure date sees the month and can pick a day

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component was passing `inputMode: !this._isInline` to Vanilla Calendar Pro, causing non-inline calendars to enable input mode which traps the Tab key inside the calendar widget, preventing focus from moving to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Set the `inputMode` option to `false` for all calendar instances to allow the Tab key to escape the calendar and move focus to the next focusable element in the form, while preserving other keyboard interactions within the calendar.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is open will move focus to the next focusable element in the form (the passengers field) instead of being trapped in the calendar.
functional_risks: Other keyboard navigation within the calendar (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) may be altered
Inline calendars may lose intended keyboard behavior if they relied on inputMode being true
verification_requirements: Verify Tab moves focus from departure date to passengers field when calendar is open
Verify arrow keys, Enter, and Escape still function correctly in the calendar
Verify inline calendars (if present) retain correct keyboard behavior

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component was passing `inputMode: !this._isInline` to Vanilla Calendar Pro, causing non-inline calendars to enable input mode which traps the Tab key inside the calendar widget, preventing focus from moving to the next form field. Additionally, the click handler for data-api toggles explicitly skipped input elements, relying solely on focusin to show the calendar, which may not fire in all test environments.
plan.repair_strategy: Set the `inputMode` option to `false` for all calendar instances to allow the Tab key to escape the calendar and move focus to the next focusable element in the form. Additionally, update the click handler to explicitly show the calendar when an input element is clicked, ensuring the calendar appears on click in all environments while preserving toggle behavior for non-input elements.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is open will move focus to the next focusable element in the form (the passengers field) instead of being trapped in the calendar. Clicking the departure date input will reliably show the calendar.
functional_risks: Other keyboard navigation within the calendar (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) may be altered if they depended on inputMode
Inline calendars may lose intended keyboard behavior if they relied on inputMode being true (but they already had inputMode: false)
The click handler change ensures inputs show the calendar on click, which matches user expectations

plan.root_cause: Three issues prevent correct keyboard and pointer behavior: (1) The datepicker passes `inputMode: !this._isInline` to Vanilla Calendar Pro, enabling input mode for non-inline calendars which traps the Tab key inside the calendar widget. (2) The data-api click handler explicitly skips input elements (`if (this.tagName === 'INPUT') return`), relying solely on focusin to show the calendar, but focusin may not fire in all test environments and the outside-click handler hides the calendar immediately after focusin. (3) The `_onOutside` dismiss handler treats the trigger element as "outside" because `element.contains(element)` returns false, causing the calendar to hide immediately when the input receives focusin from a click.
plan.repair_strategy: Make three minimal changes to js/src/datepicker.ts: (1) Set `inputMode: false` in `_buildCalendarOptions` so Tab can escape the calendar. (2) Update the data-api click handler to call `instance.show()` for input elements instead of skipping them. (3) Fix `_onOutside` in `_setupDismiss` to exclude the trigger element (`target !== this._element`) from the outside check so focusin on the trigger doesn't close the calendar.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is open moves focus to the next focusable element (passengers field) instead of being trapped. Clicking the departure date input reliably shows the calendar. Focusin on the input also shows the calendar. Non-input toggle elements still toggle the calendar.
functional_risks: Other keyboard navigation within the calendar (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) could be altered if they depended on inputMode being true
Inline calendars retain inputMode: false (unchanged behavior)

The outside-click dismiss logic now treats the trigger element as inside, which is correct for focusin but could theoretically affect pointerdown on the trigger; however pointerdown on the trigger is already handled by VCP internally

(2) The data-api click handler explicitly skips input elements, relying solely on focusin to show the calendar, but focusin may not fire in all test environments. Additionally, the click handler's `event.preventDefault()` for inputs may interfere with focusin firing in some test environments.
plan.repair_strategy: Make three minimal changes to js/src/datepicker.ts: (1) Set `inputMode: false` in `_buildCalendarOptions` so Tab can escape the calendar. (2) Update the data-api click handler to call `instance.show()` for input elements (without `event.preventDefault()`) instead of skipping them, ensuring the calendar appears on click in all environments while preserving toggle behavior for non-input elements. (3) Fix `_onOutside` in `_setupDismiss` to exclude the trigger element (`target !== this._element`) from the outside check so focusin on the trigger doesn't close the calendar.
